name: Battle of Navarino

phases.title: The Allied squadrons enter the bay
phases.text: The Ottoman and Egyptian fleet lay anchored in a horseshoe of three lines. The Allied ships came through the southern entrance in two lines, British and French to starboard and the Russians to port, slightly behind.

phases.title: The Allies anchor in the crescent
phases.text: The three British ships of the line anchored facing the Ottoman centre. The French took the side facing the Ottoman left wing, and the Russians the right end of the crescent. Allied captains had orders to fire only if attacked.

phases.title: Dartmouth's cutter is fired on
phases.text: Fellowes of Dartmouth saw an Ottoman crew preparing a fireship and sent a boat to tell them to stop. The Ottomans fired on the boat and lit the fireship, then fired on the cutter sent to tow it clear.

phases.title: The firing spreads along the line
phases.text: Fellowes opened musket fire to cover his men, and the French flagship Sirène fired to support Dartmouth. An Ottoman corvette attacked Sirène, and the shooting spread until there was a general engagement.

phases.title: A fireship jams under Scipion's bowsprit
phases.text: The French Scipion came under intense attack from Egyptian frigates, the shore batteries and a fireship. The fireship jammed under her bowsprit and set her fore sails alight; Trident towed it clear.

phases.title: The French silence the fort's battery
phases.text: Sirène, with the support of Trident and Scipion, bombarded the fort of Navarino and eventually silenced its shore battery.

phases.title: Breslaw breaks away from the French
phases.text: Seeing that Rigny did not need further support, the captain of Breslaw decided on his own initiative to leave the French formation and head for the centre of the bay.

phases.title: The centre fights at anchor
phases.text: Ships fired at very close range, with little room to manoeuvre. Asia concentrated her fire on Fahti Bahri, and Breslaw reached the junction of the British and Russian lines to reinforce Albion and Azov, both hard pressed.

phases.title: The Ottoman front line is despatched
phases.text: All three Ottoman ships of the line and most of the large frigates of the first line had been despatched. The small British and French vessels stopped the fireships, and only the first attack on Scipion got home.

phases.title: The smaller vessels are destroyed
phases.text: The Allied ships of the line, all still operational, fired on the second and third lines. Codrington tried twice to order a ceasefire, but his signals were hidden by smoke or ignored. Of 78 vessels, just eight stayed seaworthy.

note: The plan shows the bay as a schematic, not to scale. The accounts give the shape of the Ottoman line and which Allied squadron faced which part of it, but not exact anchorages. Where the Ottoman left and right wings lay on the page, and where the corvettes at the entrance stood, is placed by judgement. The Ottoman second and third lines are drawn as one block, and the Allied squadrons as one block each. The account of the fighting is a summary that does not date each action, so the order of the French actions against the fort, Breslaw's move and the fighting in the centre and on the Russian side is only partly given. Allied sources give the account of how the fighting began; Codrington's claim that the Ottomans began it is the account followed.
